descriptions.text: Donate Inflation ExchangeRate && Rounding Error. Lost: $7M

On April 15th, Hundred Finance suffered a $7.4M exploit on Optimism. This is the protocol's first solo article, after having shared the stage with both Agave DAO and Meter. With Hundred’s leaderboard total now standing at $16.9M… what was it this time?

cToken.redeem() is rounded down - first deposit bug Vulnerable code snippet: https://optimistic.etherscan.io/address/0x7100cbca885905f922a19006cf7fd5d0e1bbb26c#code#F8#L123 Attack tx: https://optimistic.etherscan.io/tx/0x6e9ebcdebbabda04fa9f2e3bc21ea8b2e4fb4bf4f4670cb8483e2f0b2604f451 Analysis: https://twitter.com/peckshield/status/1647307128267476992 https://twitter.com/danielvf/status/1647329491788677121 https://twitter.com/hexagate_/status/1647334970258608131 https://blog.hundred.finance/15-04-23-hundred-finance-hack-post-mortem-d895b618cf33

The loss of today's HundredFinance hack is ~$7m.The root cause appears the attacker donates 200 WBTC to inflate hWBTC's exchange rate so that even a tiny amount (2 wei) of hWBTC can basically drain current lending pools.

On April 15, 2023, Hundred Finance on Optimism was exploited for approximately $7.4 million. The attacker leveraged a well-documented ERC-4626 share inflation flaw by depositing a minimal amount into an empty hWBTC market, directly donating a large amount of WBTC, and borrowing inflated collateral to drain other markets. The newly migrated ERC-4626 share accounting allowed an attacker to become the sole depositor in an empty hWBTC market, then donate assets to inflate the share price.
